A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the case of a thrombotic coronary occlusion in the absence of collateral circulation, the use of an intra-aortic balloon counterpulsation may be of great help in order to improve the chances of success of a mechanical dethrombectomy.

in case of a thrombotic occlusive event in a patient with a well-developed right coronary system, a pharmacologic and mechanical dethrombotization can be attempted, and it may be a life-saving procedure, provided that the patient is supported by intra-aortic balloon pumping.

in case of acute myocardial infraction due to thrombotically occluded left main coronary artery, an aggressive dethombotic intervention, including intra-aortic balloon pumping, is mandatory, in order to achieve a successful outcome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in selected patients, the use of a combined pharmacologic and mechanical approach can be a successful and life-saving strategy in the management of acute coronary occlusion.

a combination of pharmacological and mechanical thrombolytic therapy may be a life saving strategy in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarctions and acute thrombotic occlusions of the left main coronary artery.

, in case of a massive left coronary artery thrombosis, the use of intra-arterial thrombolysis should be considered, even in the presence of contraindications, as a last resource to prevent death or severe left ventricular dysfunction.
